thread:
marie: Heads-up: staging p99 spiked after the latest model-onboard (checkpoint v2.3.1) — seeing ~2.1x latency on long-chat prompts

alex: noticed. CI perf also flagged a regression on e2e-load test (job 9456) — measured end-to-end time doubled. Stack traces point to kernel fallback / slower attention kernel.

siva: can you paste the profiler snippets? also need job id and commit.

marie: pasted small summary below from a quick profiler run:
```
p99: 190ms -> 410ms
kernel: expected "fast_attn_v2" selected but runtime fell back to "generic_attn"
batching: avg batch size 3 -> 1.2 (more small batches)
kv-cache hit-rate: 87% -> 32%
```

mia: kv-cache hit drop is suspicious — note the tokenizer changes in v2.3.1 included an EOS normalization tweak and altered prefix hashing. Could affect cache keys.

alex: CI failure page: https://ci.redwood/job/9456 — perf-regression-check flagged commit 0a1b2c3 (model-onboard + tokenizer-config bump) as suspect.

ci-bot: perf-check: regression detected on job 9456 (p99 latency +132%). Suspect change set: 0a1b2c3

marie: ran a local bisect: disabling the new eos-normalize in tokenizer restores kv-hit ~85% and p99 drops to ~200ms.

siva: that aligns: tokenizer-induced key-drift -> massive cache miss rate -> fewer batched requests (more singletons) -> runtime picks generic_attn for odd seq/batch combos -> p99 spike.

alex: action: open revert for tokenizer config and add a gating test in model-onboard pipeline that checks kv-key stability. I'll queue the revert if you confirm.

mia: opening revert PR for tokenizer config now (PR #4123). Will include canary plan.

marie: profiler trace for kernel selection attached for one sample:
```
# kernel selection trace
selected_kernel=generic_attn stack="runtime/kernel_selector:line 234"
seq_len=1024 batch=1
```

siva: also captured scheduler logs showing micro-batching fragmentation: `batch_window_us=600` which is too small under high singleton rate; increasing to 1200 reduced fragmentation in tests.

alex: question: do we also want a kernel-selection guard that forces fast_attn for compatible shapes even if cache metrics are low? Might mask underlying issues but would reduce user impact. Tradeoffs?

mia: revert opened (PR #4123). Plan: shadow-canary 10% traffic, verify kv-hit and p99, then promote. Also add regression test.

deploy-bot: Canary started: shadow=10% cluster=staging-3 (PR #4123)

marie: after revert locally + simulated traffic: p99 ~180ms (baseline ~170-190ms), kv-hit ~89% — looks good.

siva: recommendation: add a checksum comparison step in onboarding pipeline that samples N prompts and verifies produced kv-key digests against a golden (or baseline) for a small corpus. Fail onboarding if >5% keys differ.

alex: also add CI perf step: run a mini-shadow workload that exercises kv-cache and assert <=5% kv-hit delta and <=10% p99 delta before merge.

mia: agreed. I'll add tests to model-onboard pipeline and follow-up PR to gate tokenizer changes.

ci-bot: Note: perf job 9459 queued for PR #4123 (post-revert)

alex: thanks all. Holding rollout until canary green and CI perf passes.

marie: marking this thread on the incident board. Revert-blocker cleared once canary passes :white_check_mark:
